# dp_driven viz (§6)

The §6 rendering contract. Source of truth: `scripts/dp_driven_viz.py`. Design baseline:
`zj-dp-driven-skill-design.md` §6 (R1–R6), §8 (backend choice).

## Backend decision (R10, was `[未决]`)

**Mermaid `flowchart TD` text**, generated by stdlib only. Rejected alternatives and why:

| Alternative | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| static HTML + vendored dagre/elk | vendored JS bundle breaks the zero-dep stance and couples the view layer to an external asset tree |
| Graphviz `dot` + `dot -Tsvg` | needs an external binary, violating stdlib-only |
| terminal ASCII | can't cleanly express claim distinction / overlap markers / cross-plan quotient |
| IR-JSON only | doesn't actually pick a backend |

Mermaid also keeps the output **greppable/diffable text**, so every visual requirement
(R1–R6) is a failing test, not a screenshot hope.

## CLI

```bash
# mermaid text to stdout (live view)
$DP viz DB
# mermaid text to a sibling file (process zone, default <db-without-ext>.mmd; §5.4 — not durable, not git-tracked)
$DP viz DB --out docs/plans/dp-driven/<topic>/dp_driven.mmd
# R7 interactive HTML viewer (Phase-4b)
$DP viz DB --format html                        # html to stdout
$DP viz DB --format html --out <db>.html        # process zone, sibling of the carrier
$DP viz DB --format html --out <db>.html --assets inline --js-path mermaid.esm.min.mjs
# --now EPOCH overrides the clock used to evaluate claim expiry (§4.4)
```

`viz` is a **pure read** in every format: no lock, no write, no save (locked by
`test_dp_driven_viz.py::test_render_is_pure_readonly`, `test_dp_driven_viz_cli.py::
test_viz_cli_readonly`, and for the HTML surface `test_dp_driven_viz_html.py::
test_render_html_is_pure_readonly` / `test_viz_html_cli_readonly`). Rendering a
suggestion/view must never become state (§3.1/§3.6).

## Requirement → mechanism map (R1–R6)

| Req | Mechanism in the emitted Mermaid |
|---|---|
| **R1** layer-1 `tasks-state-graph` | top-level edges `T<a> -->|plan-dep| T<b>`, one per distinct cross-plan `blocks` edge (§3.6 F2 商图投影) |
| **R2** layer-2 per-plan region | `subgraph T<tid>["task<tid> <name> (<status>)"]` containing that plan's tickets/findings + intra `blocks`/`parent`/`derived_from` edges |
| **R3** simple status marker | node label `… <status>`; status class via `classDef` (see below). Blocked status is **derived** (§3.2), never read from a stored field |
| **R4** orphan findings | separate `subgraph ORPHANS[...]`; also holds unclaimed tickets (`task_id IS NULL`). A shared finding is never orphaned |
| **R5** claim distinction | `class T<tid> plan_inflight` (a real agent holds the plan claim) vs `plan_paused` (open, no claim) vs `plan_settlement` (settlement sentinel); terminal plans get no emphasis class |
| **R6** shared finding 取巧渲染 | a multi-membership finding is emitted **once per plan** (`f<id>_T<a>`, `f<id>_T<b>`) with `⟲` marker + `:::overlap`; **no** `f<id>_T<a> --> f<id>_T<b>` cross-plan overlap edges are ever drawn |

## Node identity & edges

- Node instance id: `tk<id>_T<plan>` / `f<id>_T<plan>`, or `_ORPHAN` when unplaced.
- A node may have several instances (shared finding); edges reference the **canonical**
  instance (ticket→its owner plan; finding→lowest membership plan) so each `blocks` /
  `parent` / `derived_from` edge is drawn exactly once.
- Edge syntax: `-->|blocks|` (依赖), `-->|parent|` (父子, never blocks — §3.2),
  `-.->|derived_from|` (materialization forms ①②), `-.->|origin(form-③)|`
  (finding→new task, links to the whole plan subgraph node).

## classDef contract

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| `open` / `done` / `abandoned` | stored lifecycle states |
| `blocked` | derived (§3.2) — shown but never stored |
| `overlap` | finding with >1 membership (R6, takes priority over its status color) |
| `plan_inflight` / `plan_paused` / `plan_settlement` | claim state (R5) |

Colors are GitHub-light-theme tokens; they carry no semantics beyond the class name, so a
renderer without them still shows correct topology.

## Guarantees (test-enforced)

- **deterministic** — same `(model.data, epoch)` ⇒ byte-equal text (everything iterated in sorted
  order; labels use `created_at` ordering only inside status; the module itself reads no clock —
  the `epoch` for §4.4 expiry comes from the caller, `None` in the Python API).
- **pure read** — never mutates/saves the model; writes only the single `--out` path (§5.4).
- **sanitized labels** — `"`/`[`/`]`/`{`/`}`/backtick are stripped from names so the
  generated text is always valid Mermaid.

## R7 interactive HTML viewer (Phase-4b, was `[未决]`)

Architecture (chosen over vendored-layout HTML and over Pages/deployables):

```
model (read-only)
 ├─▶ dp_driven_viz.render()          Mermaid text — R1–R6, layout/semantics source of truth
 └─▶ dp_driven_viz.build_node_ir()   per-node-instance snapshot, keys == Mermaid ids
        ▼
 dp_driven_viz_html.render_html()    single self-contained file:
      <pre class="mermaid">  = render() text (html-escaped, byte-exact)
      <script type="application/json" id="dp-ir"> = the IR snapshot
       native JS (~70 lines)  = post-render data-id backfill → click delegation on
                                g.node / g.cluster → card panel
```

- **No second layout truth**: the viewer never re-derives the graph; it embeds `render()`
  verbatim **with the same `epoch` it passes to the IR**, so the `.mmd` and the `.html` can
  never disagree (locked by `test_html_mermaid_body_matches_render` and, for expiry, by
  `test_dp_driven_wiring.py::VizClock.test_mermaid_and_html_agree_on_expired_plan`).
- **id parity is load-bearing**: `build_node_ir()` walks the *same* traversal and reuses
  the same mid helpers as `render()`; `test_ir_ids_match_mermaid_ids` fails if anyone
  adds a node to one side only.
- **Card payload**: `kind / ref_id / plan / label / display_status / shown_blocked /
  blocked+blocked_reason (absent when free, §3.2) / external_hold / md_path /
  context_md / memory_md / memberships / overlap / derived_from_finding / parent_id /
  ref / claim_agent (+claim_expired) / created_at / completed_at / summary(plan)`.
- **Claim expiry (§4.4)**: `--now EPOCH` (CLI default = wall clock; the Python API stays
  clock-free, so `render(m)` without `epoch` never judges a lease) decides whether a plan frame
  is `plan_inflight` or `plan_paused` — in **both** formats, since Phase-4d feeds `epoch` into
  `render`/`render_to_file` as well as the IR. An
  **expired** lease renders paused **but the card keeps the stale agent +
  `claim_expired: true`** — who dropped it stays visible (`test_claim_expired_surfaced_not_hidden`).
- **Assets modes**: `cdn` (default) emits `import mermaid from
  "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs"`; `inline` embeds a
  caller-supplied ESM text (`--js-path`, or env `DP_DRIVEN_MERMAID_JS`) as a JSON string
  and loads it via a Blob URL — the file then works with no network. Nothing is vendored
  into the repo.
- **XSS-safe**: every model value reaches the DOM through `textContent` only; embedded
  JSON neutralizes `</` as `<\/` so no data can close the script tag early
  (`test_html_escape_node_name`).
- **v11 id 适配 (issue #320)**: Mermaid v11 dropped `data-id` and prefixes node ids with
  `mermaid-<ts>-`, so the viewer backfills `data-id` on `g.node`/`g.cluster` after
  `await mermaid.run()`, resolving each mid against the **closed IR key set** (never
  Mermaid's id string, so it survives renderer upgrades). `nodeKey()`'s `data-id` path is
  the load-bearing hit. Structure locked by `test_html_backfills_data_id_on_render` /
  `test_html_awaits_run_before_backfill`; the browser end-to-end hit is verified by a
  one-time headless-Chrome probe (not wired into CI — the suite is stdlib Python only).
- **Zero write-back** (invariant 10 extended to views): the IR/HTML is a generation-time
  snapshot; freshness = re-run `viz`. Locked by `test_render_html_is_pure_readonly`
  (carrier bytes unchanged) and the CLI `test_viz_html_cli_readonly`.
- **Placement (§5.4)**: output goes only to `--out` (convention `<db-stem>.html` beside
  the carrier, process zone, not git-tracked).

Still open after 4b: pan/zoom chrome and cross-artifact deep links are not implemented
(click-to-inspect only); §9 metric collection remains a separate phase.
